instruction: Use LibreOffice Calc to make a spreadsheet with student names and test scores, and save it as grades.xlsx on the desktop.

metadata.explanation: Task requires creating a grades spreadsheet with student names and scores, then saving to desktop. Evaluator verifies file exists and contains actual grades data by checking for text columns (student names) and numeric columns (test scores), with minimum 2 rows and 2 columns. Custom getter reads file using env.controller.get_file(), extracts cell values with openpyxl, and validates both structure and content type. Metric verifies semantic requirements for a valid grades spreadsheet.
metadata.scoring_breakdown: Binary scoring: 1.0 if file exists and is valid, 0.0 otherwise

llm_judge_reasons: Getter correctly extracts and validates semantic content: iterates through cells to check for text columns (student names) and numeric columns (test scores) at lines 40-66
Comprehensive coverage: verifies all instruction requirements - file existence, text data (student names), numeric data (test scores), and minimum structure (2+ rows, 2+ columns)
Logic correctly distinguishes grades spreadsheet from random data: requires both has_text_column AND has_numeric_column, preventing false positives from non-grades files
Metric properly validates all semantic requirements returned by getter: checks exists, valid, has_text_column, has_numeric_column, row_count>=2, col_count>=2
Implementation is robust: handles edge cases (empty files, non-existent files, files with only text or only numbers)
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Minor enhancement: The expected.rules parameter could be used to make thresholds configurable (e.g., min_rows, min_cols), but current hardcoded values (2 rows, 2 columns) are reasonable defaults
